page: Amazon Web Services p3dn.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring eight NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs with a total of 256 GB of VRAM. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8175M processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The system includes 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, which translates to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of 1800 GB of NVMe SSD space, and the instance is built on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. The instance exhibits weak single-core CPU performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Conversely, its multi-core capabilities are strong, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and Passmark CPU extended instructions tests scoring in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, registering strong results across both small-block cached and large-block uncached read/write operations.

This hardware profile is optimized for large-scale parallel workloads. LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier performance in the top 10% for prompt processing across small, medium, and large models, as well as top-tier text generation speeds for 7B and 70B parameter models. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage and 100 Gbps networking supports high-throughput tasks, reflected in its strong static web serving and Redis SET operation benchmarks. Given the high density of GPU accelerators and dedicated CPU resources, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for massive parallel computing tasks like deep learning training, LLM inference, and high-performance computing.
description: Amazon Web Services p3dn.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for highly parallel workloads. It features eight NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs with 256 GB of total VRAM, paired with an Intel Xeon 8175M processor offering 96 vCPUs and 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance includes 1800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data highlights a distinct tradeoff: single-core CPU performance is weak, while multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are strong. The instance excels in LLM inference, achieving top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds across various model sizes. It also demonstrates strong performance in Redis SET operations and static web serving. This hardware configuration is best suited for deep learning, large-scale LLM inference, and high-throughput parallel computing tasks where multi-GPU acceleration and high network bandwidth are required.
